challenge.name: The Consent Gap
challenge.description: A new model version requires loyalty basket data, but the deployment pipeline lacks the governance controls to verify consent. #automation_alex# wants to push the automated deployment forward immediately to meet the promotion deadline, while #requirements_reuben# insists on a manual review process to ensure legal compliance. #automation_alex# is open to adding a manual approval step if it keeps the pipeline moving, but #requirements_reuben# will not accept any automated path without full audit trails.

output.content: {efficiency_emilia} believes the deployment chain should run without human intervention to meet the promotion deadline. She argues that every hour spent on manual work is an hour the promotion allocation is not optimized. The goal is to let the system handle the entire flow from model training to store ordering automatically. This approach ensures the middle aisle stock is sized correctly before the leaflet goes to print. More automation means faster responses to demand shifts and fewer bottlenecks during the busy promotion week. The team should aim for a fully hands off process where no one has to touch the pipeline. This will maximize the margin on the promotion week and reduce the risk of missing the legal duty to have reasonable stock available.
output.reclassify_reason: The text articulates a need for full automation to meet the promotion deadline and optimize margins, and doing more to achieve this hands-off state would directly satisfy the stated goal of maximizing efficiency and compliance.
